Manifest Monotonicity (Rest-Score Regression)

Source: R/26_ScaleCheck.R
ManifestMonotonicity.Rd

Checks, item by item, whether the probability of reaching each category rises with the rest score, the observable counterpart of latent monotonicity in Mokken scale analysis (Molenaar & Sijtsma, 2000; van der Ark, 2007). A single-peaked or U-shaped item, which the item-rest correlation and Scalability can show as merely weak, appears here as a run of decreases.

Usage

ManifestMonotonicity(
  U,
  na = NULL,
  Z = NULL,
  w = NULL,
  minvi = 0.03,
  minsize = NULL
)

Arguments

U

Either an object of class "exametrika" or raw data. When raw data is given, it is converted to the exametrika class with the dataFormat function.

na

Values to be treated as missing values.

Z

Missing indicator matrix of type matrix or data.frame. Values of 1 indicate observed responses, while 0 indicates missing data.

w

Item weight vector. Not used.

minvi

Smallest decrease counted as a violation. Default 0.03.

minsize

Smallest rest-score group. NULL (default) uses the rule described in Details.

Value

An object of class c("exametrika", "ManifestMonotonicity") with

ItemLabel

Item labels.

summary

Data frame, one row per item: the item scalability coefficient Hj and the totals over item steps of active pairs, violations, violations per active pair, largest violation, sum of violations, sum per active pair, largest \(z\) and number of significant violations.

groups

List, one data frame per item: rest-score range, size, category frequencies, mean item score and \(P(X \ge x)\) for each group.

violations

List, one matrix per item: the same statistics per item step, with the two groups involved in the largest \(z\).

minsize, minvi

The settings used.

n_dropped

Number of respondents dropped for missing responses.

Details

For item \(j\) the rest score \(R_{-j}\) is the sum of the other items. Respondents are sorted by rest score and cut into groups of at least minsize people, never splitting a rest score; a remainder smaller than minsize is merged into the last group. Within each group the item-step proportions \(P(X_j \ge x)\) are computed for every category \(x\) above the lowest. Manifest monotonicity requires $$P(X_j \ge x \mid R_{-j} \in \text{higher group}) \ge P(X_j \ge x \mid R_{-j} \in \text{lower group})$$ for every pair of groups. A decrease larger than minvi counts as a violation, and each violation gets the normal approximation $$z = \frac{2\left|\sqrt{(a+1)(d+1)} - \sqrt{bc}\right|}{\sqrt{n-1}},$$ where \(a\) and \(b\) are the numbers at or above and below \(x\) in the higher group, \(c\) and \(d\) the same in the lower group, and \(n = a + b + c + d\). A \(z\) above 1.6449 (one-sided 5\ multiplicity correction) is counted as significant.

The default minsize follows the mokken package: \(N/10\) for \(N \ge 500\), \(N/5\) for \(250 < N < 500\), \(N/3\) for \(N \le 250\) and 50 for \(N < 150\) (all rounded down). It is advisable to repeat the check with a few values of minsize. Below 100 respondents the default exceeds half the sample and the function stops; such a sample is too small for the regression at its default resolution, and minsize must then be chosen deliberately.

Respondents with any missing response are dropped (listwise), because a rest score over different item sets is not comparable; a message reports how many. With complete data the results agree with check.monotonicity() of the mokken package.

For polytomous items latent monotonicity does not strictly imply manifest monotonicity (Junker & Sijtsma, 2000); the check is used in practice as if it did. The function only reports; it never recodes or drops items.

References

Junker, B. W., & Sijtsma, K. (2000). Latent and manifest monotonicity in item response models. Applied Psychological Measurement, 24, 65–81.

Molenaar, I. W., & Sijtsma, K. (2000). User's manual MSP5 for Windows. IEC ProGAMMA.

van der Ark, L. A. (2007). Mokken scale analysis in R. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(11), 1–19.

Examples

# \donttest{
mm <- ManifestMonotonicity(J5S1000)
#> ManifestMonotonicity: 26 respondents with missing responses were dropped.
mm$summary
